title: The effectiveness of alternative risk assessment and program planning tools in a fraud setting
authors_or_organization: Stephen K. Asare; Arnold M. Wright
limitations: Abstract read via IDEAS/RePEc only; full text not retrieved (publisher paywall; a third-party full-text copy was not used). One case (SEC enforcement fraud case), 69 auditors, between-subjects; benchmark set by expert panel. Checklist is a tool used by the auditor in their own planning, not a coverage disclosure given to a recipient.

title: The Influence of Documentation Specificity and Priming on Auditors' Fraud Risk Assessments and Evidence Evaluation Decisions
authors_or_organization: Jacqueline S. Hammersley; E. Michael Bamber; Tina D. Carpenter
limitations: Abstract only (Crossref metadata for published and SSRN versions); participant numbers, effect sizes and design details not verified. Documentation is planning-stage documentation consumed in later audit work (intra-team handoff), not an outside advisor's report.

title: Decomposition of Fraud-Risk Assessments and Auditors' Sensitivity to Fraud Cues
authors_or_organization: T. Jeffrey Wilks; Mark F. Zimbelman
limitations: Abstract only. 52 audit managers. Decomposition is a structured judgment procedure performed by the auditor, not a recipient-facing coverage list.

title: The Influence of Judgment Decomposition on Auditors' Fraud Risk Assessments: Some Trade-Offs
authors_or_organization: Chad A. Simon; Jason L. Smith; Mark F. Zimbelman
limitations: Abstract only (Crossref). 101 experienced auditors plus two student follow-ups. Structured likelihood-magnitude decomposition, not coverage disclosure. Same research lineage as Wilks & Zimbelman (shared author) but a separate experiment.

title: Auditing Complex Estimates: How Do Construal Level and Evidence Formatting Impact Auditors' Consideration of Inconsistent Evidence?
authors_or_organization: Ann G. Backof; Tina D. Carpenter; Jane Thayer
limitations: Abstract only (Crossref); participant counts and effect sizes not verified. Manipulates a prime (consider how management arrived at the assumption) and evidence format (graph vs text), not a checklist of checks performed.

title: The Informational Value of Key Audit Matters in the Auditor's Report: Evidence from an Eye-Tracking Study
authors_or_organization: Louis-Philippe Sirois; Jean Bedard; Palash Bera
limitations: Abstract/synopsis only (Crossref); SSRN and publisher pages returned 403. Participants were accounting students (per Jarvinen et al. WP description, R3E-S07), not professional users. Abstract does not report the effect of the 'overview of audit procedures performed' format manipulation. Attention (eye fixation) is not detection accuracy.

title: Going-Concern Uncertainty and Loan Officers' Information Search Behavior: Evidence from Eye-Tracking (seminar working paper)
authors_or_organization: Tuukka Jarvinen; Emma-Riikka Myllymaki; Nina Sormunen; Laura Winther Balling
limitations: Unpublished seminar version; publication status not verified. Final sample 35 bank loan officers (Danish/Finnish banks) split across 4 cells of 8-10; eye-tracking with Tobii T120. Measures information search, not decision accuracy against a benchmark. One author affiliated with EY Finland at time of writing.

title: Risk Disclosure Preceding Negative Outcomes: The Effects of Reporting Critical Audit Matters on Judgments of Auditor Liability
authors_or_organization: Kelsey Brasel; Marcus M. Doxey; Jonathan H. Grenier; Andrew Reffett
url: https://doi.org/10.2308/accr-51380 (The Accounting Review 91(5):1345-1362); practitioner summary https://doi.org/10.2308/ciia-51546
limitations: Abstract plus Current Issues in Auditing summary abstract (Crossref); CIIA full text returned 403. Participants are mock jurors judging liability, not recipients detecting issues. Shows how evaluators read 'no CAMs' vs CAM disclosures after an undetected fraud.

title: The Forewarning Effect of Critical Audit Matter Disclosures Involving Measurement Uncertainty
authors_or_organization: Steven J. Kachelmeier; Dan Rimkus; Jaime J. Schmidt; Kristen Valentine
limitations: Abstract only. Study 1 MBA students, financial analysts, attorneys; Study 2 student mock jurors; sample sizes not verified. Measures confidence and responsibility judgments, not whether confidence reduction was appropriate (calibration).

title: Can a checklist reduce SOS errors in chest radiography?
authors_or_organization: Kevin S. Berbaum; Edmund A. Franken; Robert T. Caldwell; Kevin M. Schartz
limitations: Abstract only (Europe PMC). 20 observers, 57 radiographs; checklist condition compared with a separate earlier verbalization study using the same images (historical comparison, not randomized within one study). Reader-side checklist, not a recipient-facing coverage list.

title: The Influence of a Vocalized Checklist on Detection of Multiple Abnormalities in Chest Radiography
authors_or_organization: Kevin S. Berbaum; Elizabeth A. Krupinski; Kevin M. Schartz; et al.
limitations: Abstract only. 20 radiologists, 64 radiographs. Same lab as R3E-S10 but separate experiment. Reader-side checklist.

title: The invisible gorilla strikes again: sustained inattentional blindness in expert observers
authors_or_organization: Trafton Drew; Melissa L.-H. Vo; Jeremy M. Wolfe
limitations: Abstract only (Europe PMC full-text XML not returned). 24 radiologists; single unexpected, task-irrelevant target in last case. Shows task-directed search misses unexpected items; not about checklists or coverage statements per se.

title: Systematic viewing in radiology: seeing more, missing less?
authors_or_organization: Ellen M. Kok; Halszka Jarodzka; Anique B.H. de Bruin; et al.
url: https://doi.org/10.1007/s10459-015-9624-y (Advances in Health Sciences Education 21(1):189-205; PMC4749649)
limitations: Full text via Europe PMC. Small samples (Exp 1: 30 readers, 5 radiographs; Exp 2: 75 students). Coverage measured by eye tracking, not by a report statement. Novice-heavy for the training experiment.

title: Checklists improve experts' diagnostic decisions
authors_or_organization: Matthew Sibbald; Anique B.H. de Bruin; Jeroen J.G. van Merrienboer
limitations: Abstract only. 15 experts, 18 ECGs, within-subject conditions. Checklist used by the interpreter to verify own work, not by a downstream recipient.

title: Effects of incorrect computer-aided detection (CAD) output on human decision-making in mammography
authors_or_organization: Eugenio Alberdi; Andrey Povyakalo; Lorenzo Strigini; Peter Ayton
limitations: Abstract only. Two separate reader groups (20 with CAD, 19 without) rather than within-reader comparison; test set enriched (50% of cancers with incorrect CAD output). Automation-bias literature broadly is already in register (Goddard 2012 review); this item is used narrowly for the 'absence of a flag read as clean' mechanism.

title: Introduction of surgical safety checklists in Ontario, Canada
authors_or_organization: David R. Urbach; Anand Govindarajan; Refik Saskin; Andrew S. Wilton; Nancy N. Baxter
data_collection_dates: 3-month periods before and after each hospital's checklist adoption (Ontario, c. 2010)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Canadian Institutes of Health Research (per abstract)
limitations: Abstract only. Natural experiment with administrative data; checklist compliance/quality not observed in abstract; short pre/post windows. Mechanism analogy only (team process checklist, not coverage disclosure). Contrasts with earlier pre-post evidence (Haynes et al. 2009, NEJM, PMID 19144931: deaths 1.5% to 0.8%), noted but not separately registered.

title: Causal Analysis of World Health Organization's Surgical Safety Checklist Implementation Quality and Impact on Care Processes and Patient Outcomes: Secondary Analysis From a Large Stepped Wedge Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial in Norway
authors_or_organization: Arvid Steinar Haugen; Hilde Valen Waehle; Stian Kreken Almeland; Stig Harthug; Nick Sevdalis; Geir Egil Eide; Monica Wammen Nortvedt; Ingrid Smith; Eirik Softeland
limitations: Abstract only. Secondary analysis from one hospital of a stepped-wedge RCT; implementation quality was not randomized, so the 'high-quality implementation' contrast is observational. Mechanism analogy only.

title: Checklists to prevent diagnostic errors: a pilot randomized controlled trial
authors_or_organization: John W. Ely; Mark A. Graber
limitations: Abstract only. Pilot: 14 physicians, 100 patients, 17 diagnostic errors; underpowered; subgroup finding post hoc. Checklist used by the decision-maker, not a recipient-facing coverage list.
